properties.name: Seat identity must not rest on protocol-level MCP sessions, which the 2026-07-28 spec removes
properties.statement:
reflow2's per-client seat identity is inherited from a transport detail that the MCP specification published on 2026-07-28 deletes. This is a dated external change with a known deadline, not a preference.

WHAT THE SPEC DOES. The 2026-07-28 revision removes protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from the Streamable HTTP transport, and states the replacement: "Servers that need cross-call state use explicit, server-minted handles passed as ordinary tool arguments" (SEP-2567). It also removes the initialize / notifications/initialized handshake entirely, moving protocol version and client capabilities into per-request _meta (SEP-2575). A feature lifecycle policy guarantees at least twelve months between deprecation and removal, so nothing breaks immediately.

WHAT reflow2 RESTS ON, in its own words. crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs, on req:seat-per-client: "One server holds many client sessions — RMCP BUILDS A SERVICE PER SESSION — so a process-wide seat would report every client as the same owner and make claim_report say six sessions are each other." That per-session service construction is a consequence of protocol-level sessions. Remove them and the foundation of seat-per-client goes with it, taking a substantial cluster: cap:shared-sessions, cap:remote-sessions, cap:claim-liveness, cap:stale-seat-refusal, claim_report and the claim board they serve. The dependency is currently on rmcp = "2"; the workspace manifest already notes a local checkout tracking rmcp v3 betas, which is the likely landing point.

THE FIX IS PROBABLY AN IMPROVEMENT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT ALARM. A server-minted seat handle passed as an ordinary tool argument makes identity EXPLICIT and inspectable rather than inherited from whatever the transport happened to do — and it works identically over stdio, Streamable HTTP and any future transport, where the present arrangement quietly differs between them. It also composes with what already exists: identity.rs already mints and reads seats (mint_seat, seat_id, seat_liveness), and dec:identity-out-of-band already holds that names are assigned with zero coordination rather than derived from shared state, which is the same principle one layer up. The work is deciding how a client obtains and carries the handle without making every tool call carry a parameter no human should have to think about.

OTHER EXPOSURES FROM THE SAME REVISION, smaller and listed so they are not rediscovered: server/discover becomes MUST-implement; ping, logging/setLevel and notifications/roots/list_changed are removed; SSE resumability (Last-Event-ID) is gone, so a broken response stream loses the in-flight request; ttlMs and cacheScope become REQUIRED on tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/read and resources/templates/list; Roots, Sampling and Logging are deprecated; and tools/list SHOULD return a deterministic order.

THREE PLACES reflow2 IS ALREADY ALIGNED, worth knowing before anyone plans work. (1) The Logging deprecation prescribes logging to stderr on stdio — which tools/reflow2-mcp-launch.sh already does deliberately, because stdout is the JSON-RPC channel and a stray byte corrupts the protocol. (2) The deterministic-order SHOULD is already satisfied in practice by the toolsnap goldens, which pin the surface. (3) Most interestingly, the new Multi Round-Trip Requests pattern (SEP-2322) — a server returns InputRequiredResult and the client retries the original request carrying inputResponses — is the shape gap_to_prompt and ingest_step already implement by hand, with NO server-side session state and an abandoned handshake stranding nothing. reflow2 solved stateless elicitation before the specification standardised it; the migration there is likely renaming rather than redesign.

Found 2026-07-28, the day the specification published. Anthony's word: capture it.
